A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CostFilter-AD and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Retained material can be matched across the reorganization; numerical inconsistencies do not prevent comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original plug-in evaluations on MVTec-AD and VisA, component ablations, template compatibility experiments, and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds baseline comparisons, MPDD and BTAD evaluations, full-template experiments, and failure cases.

M1.justification: Section 3.5 changes the reported inference output from the filtered anomaly map M to a weighted combination, λM + (1−λ)Mbaseline. The cost-volume construction, filtering network, dual-stream attention, class-aware adaptor, and losses remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish whether retained experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: v3 adds multi-class anomaly detection and localization on MPDD, covering six metal-part categories, and BTAD, covering three industrial categories (Table 3 and Tables 17–20). These substantially extend the evaluated data coverage beyond the retained MVTec-AD and VisA experiments.

E2.justification: UniAD and Dinomaly become evaluated baselines and plug-in hosts on MVTec-AD and VisA. Conversely, SimpleNet and DeSTSeg comparisons in v1 Tables 7–10 are removed from the corresponding appendix comparisons. The new BTAD and MPDD tables evaluate HVQ-Trans and Dinomaly, despite appendix prose incorrectly naming UniAD.

E3.justification: Appendix D and Table 8 add full-template-bank evaluation at resolutions 256, 448, and 672, explicitly reusing models trained with three templates at 256 without retraining. These extend the evaluation design beyond the retained three-template tests. Resource evaluation also adds parameter counts and FLOPs to memory and latency measurements.

E4.justification: v3 adds tests of sensitivity to template availability and image resolution without retraining (Appendix D), plus six-category failure-case analysis (Section 4.5 and Figure 4). These examine deployment flexibility and failure conditions absent from v1. The original component ablations, hybrid-template experiment, and progressive-denoising analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The retained KDE curves and boxplots describe anomaly-logit distributions; they do not introduce new reporting of experimental uncertainty.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 retain their original AUROC values, but v3 adds extensive results for new baselines, datasets, and full-template settings. Existing appendix values also change: AnomalDF+Ours' VisA mean AUPRO changes from 84.5 in v1 Table 10 to 86.3 in v3 Table 16, although v3 Table 8 still reports 84.5. This is an unreconciled reporting change, not an established performance gain.

T1.justification: Section 3.5 adds a mathematical definition of the combined inference response, λM + (1−λ)Mbaseline, with λ in [0,1]. The cost-volume, attention, and loss formulations in Equations 1–5 remain unchanged; no new assumptions, theorems, or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The introduction generalizes its state-of-the-art performance contribution from the explicitly named MVTec-AD and VisA benchmarks to multiple benchmarks, alongside the expanded evaluation. The abstract and conclusion retain the central claims about matching-noise filtering, dual-stream guidance, and a generic plug-in for single- and multi-class UAD.

C2.justification: Section 4.5 newly explains that filtering depends on anomaly-relevant signals already present in the cost volume, with recovery difficult under low resolution or inadequate feature extraction. Appendix D interprets the added tests as generalization across resolutions and template counts without retraining. Existing matching-noise explanations are largely retained.

D1.justification: v3 newly documents direct use of input and reconstructed latent features for HVQ-Trans, UniAD, and Dinomaly, and projection into a 96-dimensional space. It clarifies dynamic template sampling and model reuse for the added tests. Most training settings remain unchanged, and both abstracts still promise future code/model release; the inference blending weight's selection remains unspecified.

R1.justification: v3 adds literature including PNI, MoEAD, Dinomaly, the new datasets, and light-field rendering work, while removing the DeSTSeg reference and associated comparison positioning. These extend the supporting literature without substantially changing the central positioning of matching-cost filtering as an overlooked opportunity in UAD.

P1.justification: Most introductory and methodological prose is retained. Local rewrites clarify inference, template sampling, and efficiency; the appendix moves quantitative sections after qualitative discussion and adds sections for the new evaluations. This is a limited narrative reorganization rather than an extensive rewrite.

P2.justification: The four original appendix benchmark tables are rebuilt into eight tables grouped by metric, with four additional BTAD/MPDD tables. v3 also adds benchmark-summary and full-template tables, expands the efficiency table, and introduces failure Figure 4. Existing architecture and qualitative figures are retained, with some resizing and relocation.

improvement.justification: Full-template tests reduce reliance on the earlier three-template comparison, while additional plug-in hosts and explicit failure conditions strengthen applicability assessment and transparency (Tables 3 and 8; Section 4.5). These provide a limited overall improvement. However, conflicting Dinomaly scores between the prose and Table 3, and conflicting AnomalDF+Ours AUPRO means in Tables 8 and 16, weaken confidence in parts of the expanded evidence.
